h: Where to start The pieces How these pages are organised
x: portcode wiki portcode is a terminal agent that studies a program, rewrites it in rust, and checks the result against the original. it is built for models you run yourself ollama, lm studio, llama.cpp, vllm, lakomoor.com/v1 , and it also works with a hosted api or with your claude code or codex subscription. what sets it apart is the proof. portcode pins the exact build of the original sha256 , writes down every fact as an observation , an inference or an unknown , ports one module at a time, and only calls a module done after a parity run passes against the original's own output. where to start if you want to… read install it install install.html pick a model and enter a key first run first run.html see what the screen shows and how to drive it a tour of the app tour.html port a program the port workflow port workflow.html look inside a binary, a unity game or a .net app clean room and deep mode modes.html , engines engines.html use your claude or chatgpt subscription claude code and codex subscriptions.html run local models well providers and models providers.html look something up slash commands commands.html , keyboard shortcuts keys.html , configuration config.html , command line cli.html the pieces agents decide what the model does: build for general work, port for the full port workflow, reverse for studying an original, plan for read only planning, and team for several workers at once. see agents agents.html . tools are everything the agent can do: read and edit files, run commands, record evidence, run parity checks, take screenshots, build the site. the app, the agent and portcode tool share one list. see tools tools.html . modes decide how closely the original may be examined. the default, clean room , only observes it from outside. deep mode may disassemble

h: 1. Open a folder 2. Pick a model and give it a key 3. Check that it works 4. Start working Settings worth knowing early
x: first run five minutes from install to your first task. 1. open a folder run portcode in the folder you want to work in. for a port, that is the folder that holds the program to port: put the original in original/ . when the prompt is empty, portcode looks at the folder and puts a guess at your first message in the prompt box as grey text. press tab to use it, esc to dismiss it, or just type something else. see a tour of the app tour.html the first message suggestion . 2. pick a model and give it a key portcode speaks the openai chat protocol, so almost any server works. choose one way: a local model, no key. start ollama, lm studio, llama.cpp or vllm, then type /provider ollama qwen3:14b . your claude or chatgpt subscription. install claude code or codex, sign in there once, then /provider claude code sonnet or /provider codex default . no key and no api bill. see claude code and codex subscriptions.html . a hosted api. type /key and paste the key. it is hidden while you type and saved in your config folder with mode 600. from a shell: portcode auth set <provider , or portcode auth set <provider from env name to read it from an environment variable. type what it does /provider lists providers and shows which still need a key /provider <name model switches provider and model /key provider asks for the api key, hidden /models lists the models the current provider serves /model <provider /<model picks a model /setup prints these steps again the model you choose is remembered for the next start. m and portcode model still win. 3. check that it works to test the model itself chat, tool calls, valid json, edits run portcode eval . 4. start working type a task, or type /create . /create asks what you want to recreate a website, a program, a game, a file format or nothing yet

h: The home screen The first-message suggestion The transcript The prompt The sidebar Permission dialog Screens beyond the chat Themes
x: a tour of the app the interface is a full screen terminal app in the style of opencode. portcode chat plain gives a plain line by line mode instead. the home screen when a session is empty you see the logo, the prompt box and a row of hints. the prompt box has a coloured bar on its left edge: the colour is the active agent. under it you see the model, the provider and the mode ▣ clean room , or a yellow ◉ deep . the first message suggestion in a fresh session, when you have not typed anything, portcode reads the folder and shows a grey, italic guess at what you want to do first, for example read this rust project, run its tests, and tell me what is unfinished or broken. the box tells you the keys: tab uses it, esc dismisses it, typing replaces it. how it works: 1. portcode lists the top level of the folder and the first entries of each subfolder and reads the first lines of a fixed list of project files: readme , cargo.toml , package.json , pyproject.toml , go.mod , makefile , cmakelists.txt and docs/spec.md . it never reads .env , keys or any other file. 2. it asks the model you already chose for one message you might send, in the language of your readme. 3. if the provider needs a key and has none, if you use a subscription backend, or if the model does not answer within 15 seconds, it falls back to a local guess based on what is in the folder an original/ folder, a cargo.toml , and so on . !note step 2 sends the folder listing and those file heads to your configured provider. set "suggest": false in portcode.json to turn the whole feature off. the transcript your messages, the agent's answers and every tool call appear in order. a tool call is one line with an icon a spinner while it runs, ✓ or ✗ after , the tool name and a short summary; the first lines of its outp

h: Resuming Managing sessions from the shell New sessions Freeing context with /compact Good to know
x: sessions and history every conversation is saved in your project, in .portcode/sessions/ as one file per session. you can leave and come back to it later. resuming command what it does portcode resume or r opens a list of this project's sessions to pick from portcode resume 2 opens session number 2 of that list portcode resume s 1762300000 opens a session by id; a unique prefix of an id is enough portcode c continues the latest session chat c , run c too /resume or /sessions in the app: the same list /resume 2 , /resume last in the app: open directly the list shows, newest first, each session's first message as its title, how long ago it was used and how many messages it holds. pick with ↑ ↓ and enter ; esc starts a new session. when a session opens, the old transcript is drawn again, including tool calls. the model's reasoning is not kept on screen. portcode run has no screen, so resume without a value is refused there: give a number or id, or use c . managing sessions from the shell new sessions /new and /clear start a fresh session. the old one stays on disk. freeing context with /compact /compact alias /summarize asks the model to write a dense summary of the whole conversation and replaces the history with it. the summary keeps the goal, decisions, files changed, commands run and their results, evidence ids and the exact next step. use it when a long session nears the model's context window, or before changing direction. the sidebar's context figure drops, and you carry on in the same session. portcode also compacts automatically when the window is nearly full; /compact just lets you do it earlier. the summary uses small model if you set one, otherwise the current model. it is not available while a request is running, and the claude code and codex backends manage

h: What asks by default Answering Rules in portcode.json Folders outside the project Allow-all Clean-room guard Secrets
x: permissions and allow all portcode keeps you in charge. a tool that changes something asks first, unless a rule says otherwise. what asks by default file edits and shell commands ask. reading, listing and searching files do not. fetching a web page asks. every question names the tool and the exact target the command, the path . read only agents plan , and the read only sub agents never ask: anything that would need approval is simply denied, and the model is told. answering key reply y or enter allow once a always allow that exact request for the rest of the session n or esc reject when several workers ask at once in team mode team.html , the dialogs queue and you answer them one after another. rules in portcode.json a rule is allow , ask or deny . for tools that take a target bash , edit , write , you can give a map of patterns; matches anything. a deny rule hides the tool from the model entirely when it applies to the whole tool. folders outside the project file tools stay inside the project folder. to let them touch other folders without asking, list them in "allowed dirs" . allow all /yolo approves every permission request without asking. while it is on, a red ⚠ allow all chip stays on screen. /yolo off ends it, and so does a new run of portcode: it is never saved. rules that say deny still deny. with claude code as the backend, allow all sets its permission mode to bypasspermissions ; turning it off returns to acceptedits . from a script, portcode run y "task" does the same for one run. !warning allow all lets the agent run any shell command and edit any file in the project without asking. use it only in a project and on a machine you trust, ideally in a throwaway folder or a container. clean room guard separately from permissions, bash refuses tools that look ins

h: Turning it on How a run goes The roles The team tool Permissions and cost
x: team mode team mode lets one agent lead a small team that works at the same time: a project manager, a tech lead, researchers, developers, a tester and a reviewer. turning it on either way adds the team agent to the tab cycle: or, for the running session, /team on and /team off . parallel is how many workers may run at once: 3 by default, 8 at most. how a run goes you switch to the team agent and describe the goal. the orchestrator does not write code itself. it follows this order: 1. plan. it asks pm for scope, steps and done criteria, and for code work techlead for a design and which files each developer owns. 2. do. it runs researchers on different questions and developers on different files together in one team call. 3. check. tester runs or writes the tests, reviewer reads the changes. failures go back to a developer with the exact error. 4. verify. the orchestrator runs the build or tests itself before it says it is done. it never takes a worker's word for it. 5. report. what each role did, the verified result, and what is left. while workers run, the transcript shows team ▸ developer: api started and team ■ developer: api done lines. the roles role reads edits job pm yes no scope, numbered steps, done criteria, risks techlead yes no design, files per developer, interfaces, the check to run researcher yes no answers one question with file:line evidence developer yes yes implements the files it was assigned tester yes tests only runs the project's tests and reports each failure reviewer yes no lists problems with severity, file:line and a fix workers get fresh context and only the tool list their role needs. the team tool the orchestrator calls one tool with up to 8 tasks: a failing worker is reported as failed with its error and does not stop the others. permissi

h: What happens Safe by construction Turning it off
x: python environments for python work the agent keeps everything in a virtual environment inside the project, never in your global python. what happens 1. the agent calls the venv tool with action: "create" . portcode runs python3 m venv .venv in the project after you approve it . 2. from then on, every bash command runs with virtual env set and .venv/bin first on path , so python , pip and pytest mean the project's own. 3. the agent installs packages with venv and action: "install" , which runs pip install inside .venv . the tool has three actions: action does status default says whether .venv exists and which python it has create creates .venv ; does nothing if it exists install installs the listed packages into .venv safe by construction package names must be plain requirements pytest =8 , requests socks ==2.32.0 . flags, urls and anything with shell characters are refused, so the model cannot pass index url or a git url. creating the environment and installing both ask for permission. the project's api key variables are removed from the environment of these commands. turning it off it is on by default. set "venv": false in portcode.json , or use /venv off for the running session /venv on to bring it back . when it is off, create explains that and bash keeps your normal path . if creation fails, the error says whether python 3 or, on debian and ubuntu, python3 venv is missing.

h: The idea Start The finish gate The tools Where the port is created Where things live An example Two sessions for a strict clean room
x: the port workflow portcode's reason to exist: port a program and prove the port behaves the same. the port agent follows the rustport method and the runtime enforces its finish line. the idea 1. pin the original. its exact build is hashed sha256 , so every later claim is about a known artifact. 2. write down facts, with their weight. each fact goes into the ledger as one of three kinds: kind meaning observation i saw or ran it. inference i worked it out from observations. unknown i do not know yet. an unknown stays open until something resolves it. portcode never claims parity without a passing parity run. 3. port one module at a time. each module is compared with golden output captured from the original , not from your port. 4. check with parity. a differential run compares the port's output with the golden files, with tolerances for floating point. 5. show it. a screenshot per feature and a generated site for github pages. start put the original in original/ and run: or type /create and answer the questions. the agent begins by reading the ledger and docs/port.md if they exist, and says which phase it is in. the finish gate port does not stop early. if any of these is true when it tries to finish, it is sent back to work and given more steps: a behaviour of the original an option, an output format, an exit code, an error message is not in the todo list, a todo is still open, the last parity run did not pass on the final code. the only exit is blocked : the agent stops and shows a needs your decision card with its questions. your answer resumes the run. the tools tool does survey inventories a source tree: languages and size, build files, engine and graphics hints, assets, tests, risk hotspots pin pins the original build sha256, size, format, version in .portcode/refe

x: remote control drive a portcode session from a browser or phone: watch the transcript, send prompts, answer permission requests, interrupt, switch agent or mode. how it works. github pages hosts only a static page /portcode/remote/ . your browser connects directly to portcode serve or /remote inside the full screen ui over a websocket. there is no portcode relay: nothing between you and your machine except the tunnel you choose. easiest: one command and a qr code serve tunnel also offers to download cloudflared the first time. it opens a free cloudflare quick tunnel no account , and prints https://lakomoor.github.io/portcode/remote/ url=wss://….trycloudflare.com&key=pc1.… . the part after never leaves your browser, and the page connects with that key. the address changes on every run, so scan the new code each time. the link contains your key: do not share it. anyone who learns the tunnel address still cannot connect without the key. quick start open https://lakomoor.github.io/portcode/remote/ , enter the address and the key. on the same machine use ws://127.0.0.1:7777 . from elsewhere you need a tunnel, because github pages is https and browsers only allow wss:// plain ws:// is allowed for 127.0.0.1 only : tunnel command address to enter tailscale private to your devices tailscale serve bg https=443 http://127.0.0.1:7777 wss://<machine .<tailnet .ts.net cloudflare quick tunnel cloudflared tunnel url http://127.0.0.1:7777 wss://<random .trycloudflare.com ssh your own server ssh n l 7777:127.0.0.1:7777 you@server ws://127.0.0.1:7777 safari blocks this; use another browser tailscale is the best default: the address is reachable only from your own devices. keys full can send prompts, answer permission asks, interrupt, switch agent/model and enable deep mode. view only wat

x: architecture layering: a crate depends only on lower layers. unsafe code = "forbid" workspace wide. input facing crates deny unwrap/expect/indexing . agent loop run.rs send text → for each step: fit context prune old tool output → summarise → chat with the agent's visible tools → push assistant message → for each tool call: loop guard, exec → push tool message → persist. exec validates the object/required params, runs the tool in its own task a panic becomes an error string , clips output to the profile limit. tool contract tool.rs name, description, schema, example, run ctx, args . ctx carries the project root, permission rules + gate, per session state files read with mtimes, todos , the ledger, cancel flag, read only flag. paths resolve lexically then via the longest existing ancestor's real path symlink escapes ask external directory ; .git is write protected; .env /keys ask secret file . permissions rules::check tool, target, default : most specific pattern wins; ties → deny ask allow. bash : hard deny list first, then explicit patterns, then a read only allowlist never when the command contains ; & < \ $ . read only agents deny edit and every prompt. subprocesses run command : sh c , stdin null, own process group, wall clock deadline, 1 mb capture per stream drained so the child never blocks , group sigkill on timeout/cancel, provider key env vars scrubbed. evidence flow pin / screenshot / evidence add → ledger → docs/port.md cites ids → site build groups evidence by subject with attached screenshots and open unknowns. screenshots are produced from captured output with its sha256 recorded; they are not drawn.

h: Layers Rules that matter Before you push Where the docs come from Releases
x: contributing portcode is a rust workspace. this page is the short version; agents.md in the repository is the full guide for people and agents. layers lower layers never import higher ones. see architecture architecture.html . rules that matter unsafe is forbidden. outside tests, no unwrap , expect or indexing on values that come from input lints enforce it in l0 to l2 . everything user visible is a tool in crates/portcode agent/src/tools . the app, the agent and portcode tool share it. tools never panic, never prompt on stdin, never hang: deadlines, capped output, errors that tell the model the fix. prompts in crates/portcode agent/prompts and the rustport skill are written for open weight models: short numbered rules, an example per tool, nothing time dependent before the date: line. tests enforce size and prefix stability. facts about an original go in the ledger as observation, inference or unknown. never claim parity without a parity pass. no secrets and no personal paths in code, tests, screenshots or docs. screenshots come from scripts/make screenshots.sh or portcode port shot , never by hand. deep tools must call ctx.need deep .. . engines install only under the engines folder, only after approval, and downloads need a published sha256. the app's state app holds no terminal i/o, so it stays testable. the event loop runs the tools. before you push if you changed how output is drawn, rerun scripts/make screenshots.sh and examples/wordstat/demo.sh . if you changed the docs, rerun scripts/build site.sh . where the docs come from the wiki pages are markdown in wiki/ and a few in docs/ . scripts/build wiki.py turns them into docs/wiki/ . the slash command table, the tool table and the command line page are generated from the code, so they stay correct. do not edit th
